discussions.name: NWS Seattle
synopsis: Dry conditions expected today with an upper level ridge positioned over the region. Areas of fog will be the main concern today and again Saturday morning before the next system arrives by Saturday evening. This system will bring light lowland rain and mountain snow to western Washington. The pattern will become more active next week as a series of systems brings widespread precipitation, gusty winds, and the potential for minor coastal flooding.
hydrology: Wetter systems moving into the region next week will start to bring some rises to area rivers. At this time, no river flooding is expected, however the Skokomish River will bear watching mid to late week.

sections.title: Synopsis
paragraphs: Dry conditions expected today with an upper level ridge positioned over the region. Areas of fog will be the main concern today and again Saturday morning before the next system arrives by Saturday evening. This system will bring light lowland rain and mountain snow to western Washington. The pattern will become more active next week as a series of systems brings widespread precipitation, gusty winds, and the potential for minor coastal flooding.

sections.title: Short term (today through Sunday)
paragraphs: A ridge will build into the region today as an upper level low over Oregon and northern California moves off to the south and east. Conditions are cool out there this morning with temperatures trending in the low to mid 30s as of 1AM/09Z. A few spots, especially areas south of the Sound, may see morning lows dip down into the upper 20s. Areas of fog have also started to develop across the Chehalis Valley this morning with light winds and ample moisture in the low levels. Freezing fog is likely for colder spots across the Southwest Interior overnight, with fog expected to expand further northward across Puget Sound through the early morning hours. Dry conditions are expected with the ridge overhead, with fog expected to lift and scatter by the afternoon. Afternoon highs will be in the mid to upper 40s across the interior and into the low 50s along the coast today.

Another round of fog (and freezing fog) is expected by Saturday morning, with lows expected to dip back into the upper 20s to mid 30s across the area. The ridge will then push further inland in the morning, allowing for an upper level low to drop southward from the NE Pacific and position itself offshore through Sunday. This system will bring the next round of light rain to the lowlands and light snow to the mountains. Rain will approach the coast by late Saturday morning and then gradually push inland into the interior by late afternoon. Overall rainfall amounts will remain rather light through Sunday, with only a few hundredths of an inch expected for the interior lowlands and around a tenth of an inch expected along the Central Coast. With snow levels hovering around 2000 ft, could even see some light snow accumulations (less than 1 inch) at the Cascade passes. Afternoon high temperatures both days will be in the mid 40s to low 50s. Lastly, high astronomical tides over the weekend may bring the potential for some minor coastal flooding along the Pacific Coast and the Strait of Juan de Fuca by Sunday.

sections.title: Long term (Sunday night through Thursday)
paragraphs: The low situated offshore will eventually become absorbed into the mean flow on Monday as a broad upper level low drops down into the NE Pacific from the Aleutians. This low will then deepen offshore Monday night into Tuesday and will bring a more active pattern to western Washington as the system swings a number of disturbances across the region. Expect multiple rounds of widespread lowland rain, mountain snow, and gusty winds through the second half of the week. Additionally, high astronomical tides combined with the weather impacts from these systems, will increase the threat for coastal flooding - most notably along the Pacific Coast as large waves build along the coast Tuesday into Wednesday.

sections.title: Aviation
paragraphs: Latest satellite obs show fog has developed over the southern interior bringing LIFR conditions and is starting to fill northwards across Puget Sound. Latest high-res guidance continues to suggest a 40-60 for visibility less than 1SM this morning for Puget Sound terminals. Additionally, some locations, across the southern interior (OLM) are reporting temperatures below freezing, therefore freezing fog will remain a possibility this morning. Improvement to VFR expected after 18-20Z for terminals impacted by fog. Mid to high clouds should help limit fog formation Saturday morning to the southern interior (OLM). Light to calm winds this morning, will increase this afternoon to 5-6 kt.

KSEA...LIFR cigs this morning. Satellite shows the fog starting to form within the vicinity of SEA and it is highly likely to impact the terminal. There is a 55% chance for visibility less than 1SM between 12Z-18Z. VFR this afternoon once the fog scatters out. Mid to high clouds will move in this afternoon and should help limit fog from developing Saturday morning. Light southeasterly winds this morning at 5 kt or less, increasing to 5-7 kt this afternoon.

sections.title: Marine
paragraphs: Generally benign marine conditions today with weak high pressure over the waters. Fog may form over the interior waters, with highest chances over Puget Sound this morning. Latest high-res guidance suggests portions of the Central and South Sound has a 50-60% chance for seeing visibilities less than 1 NM.

A low pressure system offshore will bring elevated seas and winds to the waters starting as early as tonight through this weekend. A Small Craft Advisory has been issued for the coastal waters and West Portion of the Strait of Juan de Fuca. Additionally, as the front associated with the parent low passes over the coastal waters, winds will increase toward gale force over the outer waters Saturday morning. With latest high-res probabilities around 50-70%, a Gale Watch has been issued for the outer coastal waters. As for the inner coastal waters, confidence is much lower for gale force gusts, but may see an occasional gale gust. Seas will build towards 10-13 feet by Sunday.

An active weather pattern will continue next week. A stronger system will impact the waters Monday into Tuesday. Increased offshore winds are highly likely to bring additional headlines. Confidence continues to increase for the potential for gales and storm force winds over the coastal waters. Latest model guidance now highlights probabilities higher than 70% for gales starting late Monday morning. Winds look to peak early Tuesday morning, with high confidence (90% and higher) for gales and a 45-70% chance for storm force winds over the outer coastal waters. Additionally, there is a 50-70% chance for gales through the Strait of Juan de Fuca on Tuesday and a slight chance (35-40%) for an isolated storm force gust through the Central and East Strait. Seas will build towards 20 feet over the outer coastal waters, with probabilities suggesting a 25-35% chance for seas exceeding 20 feet.

Additional headlines are favored midweek into late in the week, with a 70-100% chance of small craft winds over the coastal waters and Strait of Juan de Fuca. Seas are likely to remain elevated as well, with probabilities above 70% for seas greater than 10 feet and a 40- 70% for seas greater than 15 feet.

sections.title: Hydrology
paragraphs: Wetter systems moving into the region next week will start to bring some rises to area rivers. At this time, no river flooding is expected, however the Skokomish River will bear watching mid to late week.

discussions.name: NWS Portland
synopsis: A brief period of dry, calm weather will prevail today under transient high pressure before an active pattern returns this weekend. A series of Pacific frontal systems will bring multiple rounds of rain and mountain snow starting Saturday and continuing through next week. While exact details remain subject to ensemble spread, there is a low 5-10% probability of a stronger low tracking close enough to bring higher impact winds during the middle of next week.

sections.title: Synopsis
paragraphs: A brief period of dry, calm weather will prevail today under transient high pressure before an active pattern returns this weekend. A series of Pacific frontal systems will bring multiple rounds of rain and mountain snow starting Saturday and continuing through next week. While exact details remain subject to ensemble spread, there is a low 5-10% probability of a stronger low tracking close enough to bring higher impact winds during the middle of next week.

sections.title: Discussion
paragraphs: Now through Thursday...Tranquil conditions across the Pacific Northwest will give way to a prolonged, active stormy period heading into the weekend and persisting through Thanksgiving week. Shortwave ridging maintains quiet weather today, but a series of digging Gulf of Alaska troughs will drive progressive frontal systems onshore starting Saturday. This initiates a moisture-laden pattern characterized by frequent lowland rain, mountain snow accumulation, and blustery conditions at times through next week. Ensemble cluster analysis indicates considerable spread by mid-week regarding the price track and depth of offshore troughs, maintaining a low- probability scenario for stronger winds while keeping high confidence in wet weather overall.

Mountain pass travel hazards will increase starting Saturday afternoon as a cold front moves inland and snow levels drop to 2000 to 3500 feet across the Cascades. Accumulations over a 48-hour window favor light to moderate snow amounts, with a 30-50% chance of reaching 2 inches at pass levels such as Government Camp, Santiam Pass, and Willamette Pass. Higher accumulations are expected above 5000 feet within the Cascades. Motorists traveling through the Cascade passes should prepare for winter driving conditions at times over the weekend.

Precipitation spreads across southwest Washington and northwest Oregon late tonight into Saturday, bringing the first of several wet frontal passages. Rainfall amounts will vary be geography, with 48-hour exceedance probabilities for over 0.50 inches exceeding 70% along the coast, running 40-60% across the Coast Range, and 10-30% across the interior lowlands. Additional reinforcing systems will maintain high rain chances across the region through early next week.

Before the active weather arrives, clear skies and light winds early this morning will promote another round of valley fog and low stratus development. The primary impacts will be felt along the I-5 corridor in southwest Washington, the Portland metro area, and throughout the Willamette Valley, where visibility could drop significantly during the morning commute. Coastal valleys and localized spots in the southern Willamette Valley may also see patchy fog. Any frost potential will remain limited to elevated surfaces. Lows will drop into the lower 30s inland and mid 30s at the coast. Daytime highs will generally reach the mid to upper 40s across the interior lowlands and lower 50s along the coast.

Looking toward the middle of next week, active weather continues as another digging trough approaches the region from Tuesday through Thursday. The majority of ensemble members favor a robust low developing well offshore, which would mitigate severe wind impacts across southwest Washington and northwest Oregon. However, cluster guidance continues to highlight lingering variance, with a small 5-10% of members showing a more eastward tracking low that could introduce stronger, potentially damaging winds to the area. An alternate secondary meso-low scenario along the front also remains on the table for the coast. Upcoming model runs will be critical in resolving these mesoscale details as Thanksgiving approaches.  ~12

sections.title: Aviation
paragraphs: Through 12Z Saturday...High pressure today has resulted in calm winds and a low stratus deck over the Willamette Valley and Portland metro with areas of dense fog developing as of 11Z Fri. While most terminals are under MVFR CIGs and only a few under LIFR conditions, all inland terminals are expected to observe LIFR to IFR conditions early this morning, at least briefly. Recent guidance suggests the best chances of such deteriorated conditions will be between 14-20Z Fri (30-50% chance of LIFR/IFR conditions, with even higher chances of around 70% at KHIO and KUAO). Given the low sun angle this time of year, fog and low stratus will struggle to clear out in the afternoon. While most TAF sites should see improvement to VFR by 19-22Z Fri, some TAF sites may not clear out at all tomorrow, especially KEUG. Winds remain light and variable through the period.

At the coast, light offshore winds continue to try to maintain VFR conditions at KAST and KONP. Guidance suggests chances of MVFR conditions increasing to around 30% from now until 21Z Fri, with KAST's most recent observation already showing visibility reduced to 5 SM.

KPDX AND APPROACHES...Current MVFR conditions may decrease to LIFR/IFR fog/low stratus between 14-19Z Fri, with guidance suggesting a 30-40% chance of LIFR and a 50% chance of IFR. Expect conditions to improve through the late morning, improving to MVFR around 19Z Fri and then VFR by 22Z Fri. Winds remain light and variable through the period. ~12

sections.title: Marine
paragraphs: High pressure over the region continues to maintain northerly winds over the waters this morning. Seas have decreased to 6-78 ft this morning and will persist through tonight.

The next system arrives late tonight into Saturday, returning breezy southerly winds and small craft wind gusts up to 30 kt. As a result, Small Craft Advisories have been issued for the outer waters beginning 10 PM today, then expanded into the inner waters by 4 AM Saturday. By 7 AM Saturday, there is a 30-50% chance for isolated gale force wind gusts up to 35 kt across the outer waters beyond 10-20 NM offshore, and a 15-30% chance for the inner waters and Columbia River Bar, therefore a Gale Watch has been issued for the outer waters beginning at 7 AM Saturday.

Seas gradually build over the weekend as another westerly swell moves in, with high confidence (>90% chance) for seas building to 10 ft or greater, and a 20-40% chance for seas of 15 ft or greater late Saturday into early Sunday. Active weather continues next week.
Long period swells will also result in a moderate threat for sneaker waves through this weekend. Those visiting the coast should use extra precaution when in or near the water. ~12/10
